critic.verdict:
PASS WITH GAPS — the expansion is genuinely strong and current, but has systematic, fixable holes worth a targeted second pass.

Evidence basis: I merged the live corpus (Targets/Robotics/Resources/glossary_robotics.json, 1,031 entries) with the new authored chunks (docs/superpowers/specs/robotics-chunks/*.json) and audited the full per-category term lists, then ran word-boundary presence probes for ~250 candidate terms across all 20 categories.

What's excellent: the foundational/canonical vocabulary is well covered in every category (kinematics/dynamics is near-complete; control, perception, planning, sensing are thorough), and the corpus is impressively up-to-date on the 2024-2026 wave (VLA models, diffusion policy, occupancy networks, Gaussian splatting/NeRF, RSS, SOTIF, ODD, ISO/TS 15066, event cameras, quasi-direct drive). Per-category add-targets were all met or exceeded.

The single biggest structural gap is named entities: a whole class of standard datasets/benchmarks/simulators (ALOHA, DROID, Meta-World, Habitat, ManiSkill) and the post-RT-X model families (pi0, GR00T, Octo, LeRobot) is essentially absent, even though their conceptual scaffolding is present — this is the highest-leverage fix because these names dominate current robot-learning discourse. The second tier of gaps is breadth-within-covered-areas: elementary mechanical components (gear types, U-joints, bushings), discrete/contact sensors (limit switch, bumper, cliff, potentiometer), task-level manipulation verbs (insertion, singulation, deformable/cloth/cable manipulation), HRI/teleop modalities (haptics, leader-follower, BCI, AR/MR), advanced legged control (MPPI, iLQR, footstep planning, push recovery), ROS 2 build/runtime infra (colcon, QoS, lifecycle nodes, Docker/OTA), embedded buses (CAN/I2C/UART), and several standards (FMEA, HAZOP, STPA, UL 4600, ISO 3691-4, ISO/SAE 21434) plus underrepresented company segments (warehouse-logistics vendors, arm/research-hardware suppliers, the 2025-26 humanoid challenger cohort). None of these is a fundamental design flaw; they are coverage-completeness items. Recommend a focused ~120-180 term follow-up pass prioritizing the named-entity dataset/model/platform class first.
